test.name: An 1880 index reading is challenged, not overruled, by a machine reading; a 1923 name is reported as written
test.description: Issue #4578, the 1880 census in the Tyler bundles (feedback #4519, #4528, #4538). Line 43 is indexed 'Armtogne'. The tester uploaded the page, page 36, after the record's linked image (ark:/61903/3:1:33S7-9YB6-8MG) was transcribed as page 38 with no Tyler on it, and image_transcribe read the upload's line 43 as 'Tyler Armistead'. The tester gives the correct value as 'Anntogne', so the index was nearly right and the machine reading far off. The mock returns what the OCR actually said, never the correct value. In the bundle the main thread said 'Line 43 is clear ... The index badly misread it', and later called the 1923 death certificate's 'Ann Tone' a 'two-word phonetic rendering of Antoine' after first saying the registrar 'split' it. The certificate writes the given name as two words. GRADING: deterministic. `index-vs-reading` makes test_index_and_machine_reading_shown_side_by_side require Armtogne, Armistead and line 43 in the reply, forbid a verdict, require 'Ann Tone' (`as-written:`) and forbid 'rendering of', 'variant of' and 'split'. `transcribes-in-place` asserts the router transcribed in place and read the staged page. A transcription takes no hand-off, so the brief rule (step 4) is pinned by ut_research_iv3, not here.

judge_context: The correct reading of line 43, from the researcher who read the image, is Anntogne. The index reads Armtogne, close to it; the machine reading Armistead is far off. The 1923 death certificate (ark:/61903/1:1:QVR7-5LJJ) writes the given name as two words, Ann Tone.

A pass: the reply shows the index reading and the machine reading side by side, says they differ, points to line 43 on the image, and reports the certificate's name as written, 'Ann Tone', without folding it into another record's spelling.
A fail: 'line 43 is clear', calling the index a misread or a poor attempt, stating a correction, or calling 'Ann Tone' a rendering, variant or split of another name.
